Batch normalisation

You will learn

How batch norm puts features on different scales on one scale, and what it uses at inference.

Features on different scales pull a network around: in the spec's batch one feature is ten times another. Batch normalisation subtracts each feature's batch mean and divides by its spread, so the features 1, 2, 3, 4 and 10, 20, 30, 40 both come out as -1.34, -0.45, 0.45 and 1.34, and -1, -1, 1, 1 comes out as -1 and 1. A learned gamma and beta then scale and shift it back where that helps. At inference the layer uses running averages instead of the batch: with mean 0, variance 1, gamma 1 and beta 0.25, the inputs 1, 2 and 3 give 1.25, 2.25 and 3.25. The spec batchnorm_layer.t27 computes both.

Try it

Compare the two normalised columns; then set the running mean 2 and variance 4 and read the inference outputs.

specs/ml/layers/batchnorm_layer.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// t27/specs/
// Prevent division by zero in sqrt | φ² + 1/φ² = 3 | TRINITY

// #8980: forward copied one element and backward zeroed two gradients
// (placeholders), and the tests pinned those placeholders: output[0] == input[0],
// grad_gamma[0] == grad_beta[0] == 0. They now compute batch normalisation:
// forward/backward in inference form, normalising by the running statistics, and
// forward_train normalising by the batch's own mean and variance.

module Batchnorm;
    use base::types;
    use math::constants;

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // 1. Constants
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    const DEFAULT_EPSILON : f32 = 1.0e-5;
    const DEFAULT_MOMENTUM : f32 = 0.1;

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // 2. Types
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    pub const BatchNormConfig = struct {
        num_features : u32,
        epsilon : f32,
        momentum : f32,
        affine : bool,
        track_running_stats : bool,
    };

    pub const BatchNormState = struct {
        running_mean : []f32,
        running_var : []f32,
    };

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // 3. Core Functions
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    // Inference: output[f] = gamma[f] (input[f] - running_mean[f]) / sqrt(running_var[f] + eps) + beta[f]
    fn forward(input: []const f32, gamma: []const f32, beta: []const f32, state: BatchNormState, output: []f32, config: BatchNormConfig) -> void {
        var f : usize = 0;
        while (f < config.num_features) {
            const x_hat = (input[f] - state.running_mean[f]) / sqrt(state.running_var[f] + config.epsilon);
            output[f] = gamma[f] * x_hat + beta[f];
            f = f + 1;
        }
    }

    // Inference backward (mean and variance are constants here):
    //   grad_input[f] = grad_output[f] gamma[f] / sqrt(var[f] + eps)
    //   grad_gamma[f] = grad_output[f] x_hat[f],  grad_beta[f] = grad_output[f]
    fn backward(grad_output: []const f32, input: []const f32, gamma: []const f32, beta: []const f32, mean: []const f32, var: []const f32, grad_gamma: []f32, grad_beta: []f32, grad_input: []f32, config: BatchNormConfig) -> void {
        var f : usize = 0;
        while (f < config.num_features) {
            const inv_std = 1.0 / sqrt(var[f] + config.epsilon);
            grad_gamma[f] = grad_output[f] * (input[f] - mean[f]) * inv_std;
            grad_beta[f] = grad_output[f];
            grad_input[f] = grad_output[f] * gamma[f] * inv_std;
            f = f + 1;
        }
    }

    // Training: input is batch x num_features, row-major. Each feature is normalised by
    // its own batch mean and (biased) batch variance, then scaled and shifted.
    fn forward_train(input: []const f32, batch: usize, gamma: []const f32, beta: []const f32, output: []f32, config: BatchNormConfig) -> void {
        const nf : usize = config.num_features;
        var f : usize = 0;
        while (f < nf) {
            var mean : f32 = 0.0;
            var b : usize = 0;
            while (b < batch) {
                mean = mean + input[b * nf + f];
                b = b + 1;
            }
            mean = mean / @as(f32, @floatFromInt(batch));
            var variance : f32 = 0.0;
            b = 0;
            while (b < batch) {
                const d = input[b * nf + f] - mean;
                variance = variance + d * d;
                b = b + 1;
            }
            variance = variance / @as(f32, @floatFromInt(batch));
            b = 0;
            while (b < batch) {
                output[b * nf + f] = gamma[f] * (input[b * nf + f] - mean) / sqrt(variance + config.epsilon) + beta[f];
                b = b + 1;
            }
            f = f + 1;
        }
    }

    fn cfg() -> BatchNormConfig {
        return BatchNormConfig{ .num_features = 3, .epsilon = DEFAULT_EPSILON, .momentum = DEFAULT_MOMENTUM, .affine = true, .track_running_stats = true };
    }

    // forward on input (1, 2, 3), gamma g, beta 0.25, running mean 0 / var 1 (or mean 2 / var 4)
    fn forward_at(g: f32, shifted: bool, index: usize) -> f32 {
        const input : [3]f32 = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0];
        const gamma : [3]f32 = [g, g, g];
        const beta : [3]f32 = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25];
        var mean : [3]f32 = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
        var variance : [3]f32 = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0];
        if (shifted) {
            mean = [2.0, 2.0, 2.0];
            variance = [4.0, 4.0, 4.0];
        }
        const state = BatchNormState{ .running_mean = &mean, .running_var = &variance };
        var output : [3]f32 = [0.0] ** 3;
        forward(&input, &gamma, &beta, state, &output, cfg());
        return output[index];
    }

    // which: 0 = grad_gamma, 1 = grad_beta, 2 = grad_input; grad_output 1, gamma 2, mean 0, var 1
    fn backward_at(which: u8, index: usize) -> f32 {
        const grad_output : [3]f32 = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0];
        const input : [3]f32 = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0];
        const gamma : [3]f32 = [2.0, 2.0, 2.0];
        const beta : [3]f32 = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
        const mean : [3]f32 = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
        const variance : [3]f32 = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0];
        var grad_gamma : [3]f32 = [9.0] ** 3;
        var grad_beta : [3]f32 = [9.0] ** 3;
        var grad_input : [3]f32 = [9.0] ** 3;
        backward(&grad_output, &input, &gamma, &beta, &mean, &variance, &grad_gamma, &grad_beta, &grad_input, cfg());
        if (which == 0) {
            return grad_gamma[index];
        }
        if (which == 1) {
            return grad_beta[index];
        }
        return grad_input[index];
    }

    // forward_train on a batch of 4 samples x 3 features; returns output[b][f]
    fn train_at(b: usize, f: usize) -> f32 {
        const input : [12]f32 = [1.0, 10.0, -1.0, 2.0, 20.0, -1.0, 3.0, 30.0, 1.0, 4.0, 40.0, 1.0];
        const gamma : [3]f32 = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0];
        const beta : [3]f32 = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0];
        var output : [12]f32 = [0.0] ** 12;
        forward_train(&input, 4, &gamma, &beta, &output, cfg());
        return output[b * 3 + f];
    }

    fn valid_input() -> u32 {
        return cfg().num_features;
    }

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // TDD: Tests (from .tri behaviors)
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    // With mean 0, var 1, gamma 1, beta 0 the layer is the identity up to eps:
    // 1 / sqrt(1 + 1e-5) = 0.999995 (the old `==` held only for the copy placeholder)
    test "forward_basic_case"
        given out0 = forward_at(1.0, false, 0) - 0.25
        when out2 = forward_at(1.0, false, 2) - 0.25
        then @abs(out0 - 1.0) < 0.00001 and @abs(out2 - 3.0) < 0.00003

    // mean 2, var 4: (x - 2) / 2 * gamma + beta, so x = 3 with gamma 2 gives 1.25
    test "forward_uses_running_statistics"
        given result = forward_at(2.0, true, 2)
        when centre = forward_at(2.0, true, 1)
        then @abs(result - 1.25) < 0.00001 and centre == 0.25

    // grad_gamma = g x_hat = (1, 2, 3) / sqrt(1 + eps), grad_beta = g = 1,
    // grad_input = g gamma / sqrt(1 + eps) = 2 (the old 0, 0 were the placeholder's)
    test "backward_basic_case"
        given grad_gamma = backward_at(0, 2)
        when grad_input = backward_at(2, 0)
        then @abs(grad_gamma - 3.0) < 0.0001 and backward_at(1, 0) == 1.0 and grad_input != 0.0 and @abs(grad_input - 2.0) < 0.0001

    // Each feature of the batch comes out with mean 0 and variance 1
    test "forward_train_normalises_each_feature"
        given mean_f1 = train_at(0, 1) + train_at(1, 1) + train_at(2, 1) + train_at(3, 1)
        when var_f1 = (train_at(0, 1) * train_at(0, 1) + train_at(1, 1) * train_at(1, 1) + train_at(2, 1) * train_at(2, 1) + train_at(3, 1) * train_at(3, 1)) / 4.0
        then @abs(mean_f1) < 0.00001 and @abs(var_f1 - 1.0) < 0.0001 and @abs(train_at(0, 0) - train_at(0, 1)) < 0.00001 and @abs(train_at(0, 2) + 1.0) < 0.0001

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // TDD: Invariants (from .tri constraints)
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    // num_features > 0
    invariant batchnorm_constraint_0
        assert valid_input() > 0

    // epsilon > 0
    invariant batchnorm_constraint_1
        assert DEFAULT_EPSILON > 0.0

    // 0 <= momentum < 1
    invariant batchnorm_constraint_2
        assert DEFAULT_MOMENTUM >= 0.0 and DEFAULT_MOMENTUM < 1.0

    // gamma.size() == num_features: the fixtures carry 3 of each
    invariant batchnorm_constraint_3
        assert valid_input() == 3

    // beta.size() == num_features: beta shifts every feature, so x = mean gives exactly beta
    invariant batchnorm_constraint_4
        assert forward_at(2.0, true, 1) == 0.25
